title: Bridal Shower Photo Ideas: 30 Shots, Backdrops and Displays
description: Bridal shower photo ideas: a 30-shot list, 10 photo op and backdrop setups, display ideas, daylight lighting tips and how to collect everyone’s photos.
dek: A shot list for the day, setups that photograph well and everyone’s photos in one place.
excerpt: A 30-photo shot list from the dessert table to the generations portrait, 10 backdrop ideas, displays of the couple through the years, daylight tips and how to gather every guest’s photos.

faq.q: What photos should you take at a bridal shower?
faq.a: Cover four things: the details before guests arrive (invitation, dessert table, a place setting), the bride’s reactions as she opens gifts, the people (a full group photo early, a generations portrait, the bride with each friend group and the hosts), and a few candids mid-game. A written list of about 30 shots, handed to one friend, makes sure nothing gets missed.

faq.q: How do you set up a bridal shower photo booth?
faq.a: Pick a plain wall next to a window, add one backdrop such as fabric streamers, a greenery trellis or a balloon garland in two or three shades, and set out a small table of props tied to the couple’s story. Put a phone on a tripod with a timer or a booth app that counts down, and tape a mark on the floor where guests should stand.

faq.q: What can you display at a bridal shower?
faq.a: Photos of the couple through the years work best: a clothesline timeline with one photo per year, then-and-now pairs, their love story in five frames, or a wall of parents’ and grandparents’ wedding photos. A guess-the-baby-photo board doubles as a game. Set displays near the dessert table, where guests naturally gather and linger.

faq.q: Who takes the pictures at a bridal shower?
faq.a: Usually a friend, or a co-host who isn’t running the games, unless you hire a photographer. Give that person a written shot list so they can enjoy the party between shots, and let every other guest contribute through one shared album link or a shared camera QR code. The bride shouldn’t be the one taking photos at her own shower.

faq.q: How do you get photos from bridal shower guests?
faq.a: Give everyone one place to put them before the shower starts: a shared album link or a shared camera app on a QR code at the welcome table. Group chats work in a pinch, but photos get buried and saving them one at a time is slow. If you use a shared camera with a delayed reveal, print the reveal date on the favor tags.
